audit.whatIsWrong: Multiple lines call Volibear's E (Sky Splitter) a stun — "his E point-and-click stun", "Use E lightning stun to lock Tahm Kench in place", "with E stun to counter-lock your own carries", "activate Thick Skin into his E lockdown".
audit.why: Sky Splitter is a ground-targeted lightning bolt that damages and SLOWS, and shields Volibear if he stands in the blast. His only stun is Thundering Smash (Q). Telling a Tahm Kench to save Thick Skin for an E "stun" makes him hold the shield for the wrong ability and eat the real Q stun-dash with grey health uncashed.
audit.corrected: Sky Splitter (E, 16s flat) = slow + self-shield if he is inside the radius. Thundering Smash (Q, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) = the stun. Pop Thick Skin into the Q, not the E.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and content.whys[4] tell the player to use "Abyssal Voyage" to "roam or reposition globally".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's REMOVED pre-2020 W (the global two-man ferry). His current W is Abyssal Dive — a 1000/1050/1100/1150/1200-range dive that knocks up, on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown. There is no global tool in the kit at all. A player who reads this expects a map-wide escape at level 6 and will stand in a losing 50-50 waiting for an ability that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive (W) is a short-range knockup engage/disengage on a 21s cooldown at rank 1 — not a global. Level 6 gives you Devour, not map presence.

audit.whatIsWrong: The core combo is written as "Tongue Lash stun into Devour" / "stun then Devour him mid-wave" / "stun and Devour him away from his minions".
audit.why: An Acquired Taste stacks are a single shared resource. Riot's Q text: "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." Riot's passive text: "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion." The Q stun eats the three stacks, so Devour is unavailable immediately after it. The advertised combo cannot be executed off one stack set — a player who commits expecting a stun-into-eat is left standing next to Volibear with an ultimate he cannot cast.
audit.corrected: Three stacks is one charge spent on EITHER the Tongue Lash stun OR Devour. Against Volibear, Devour is the better spender — it removes him from the wave for the full duration instead of a short stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.why: Stormbringer is Volibear's R. His passive is The Relentless Storm (stacking attack speed that eventually adds bonus magic damage to nearby enemies). Naming the ult as the passive makes the whole line unreadable as a threat cue.
audit.corrected: The Relentless Storm is the passive; Stormbringer is the R that leaps and disables towers.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says he dives "under his R shield".
audit.why: Stormbringer grants bonus HEALTH, not a shield. The shield in Volibear's kit is on Sky Splitter (E) and only applies if he is standing inside his own blast radius. That distinction matters: bonus health is grey-health-farmable for Tahm Kench and does not decay, whereas the E shield does — and you can bait the E shield by not standing in it.
audit.corrected: R grants bonus health on landing; the shield is on E and only if he is inside his own blast.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Thundering Smash but gives no numbers, so "track it" is unactionable.
audit.why: The real window is concrete: Thundering Smash is 12s at rank 1 and only 10s at rank 5, Frenzied Maul is a flat 5s (his heal), Sky Splitter is a flat 16s. The punish window after a whiffed Q is roughly ten seconds at every rank — long enough for the full three-stack pattern, and the number is what makes a player actually commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early asserts "he has no gap-closer until level 2".
audit.why: Volibear can put his first point in Thundering Smash and have the stun-dash at level 1. The claim is a build assumption stated as a rule, and level 1 is exactly where a Tahm Kench who believes it will over-extend for stacks.
audit.corrected: He has a gap-closer at level 1 IF he levelled Q — read his first ability instead of assuming.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is titled "Anti-heal his W heal" but its body text is about Thundering Smash being wasted — the description does not match its own heading.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul is the heal and it is a flat 5s cooldown, re-cast on an already-marked target for bonus damage plus healing. That is the ability Grievous Wounds is bought for, and the do-line should say so.
audit.corrected: Point the anti-heal do-line at Frenzied Maul and its 5s re-bite.

audit.why: 52.32% over 753 games — an even lane. diff EVEN and diffRating 6/10 match the number; no change needed.

edits.before: At level 1 your Tongue Lash range lets you slow Volibear every time he steps up for last-hits — he has no gap-closer until level 2, so you can freely fish for the first two An Acquired Taste stacks without committing to range. The moment he hits 2 and his Q empowered dash comes online, respect the engage: he can close instantly and his passive storm procs amplify every auto during the dash window. Your answer is Tongue Lash into him the instant he winds up the Q dash, applying a slow and ideally the third stack mid-dash so your stun lands as he arrives, then Devour immediately. Landing this once at level 3 usually burns his Flash and sets the tone for the whole lane — miss it and you take a full empowered-auto chain into your face.
edits.after: At level 1 your 900-range Tongue Lash slows Volibear every time he steps up for last-hits — he only has a gap-closer if he levelled Q, so read his first ability before you fish for the first two An Acquired Taste stacks at range. Once Thundering Smash is up, respect the engage: it closes instantly and stuns, and his Relentless Storm procs amplify every auto during the dash window. Your answer is Tongue Lash the instant he winds up the Q dash, slowing the arrival and landing the third stack — then pick one spender, because the Q stun consumes all three and leaves nothing for Devour. Devour is the better punish at level 3: it usually burns his Flash and sets the tone for the whole lane.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the honest part of this matchup: Volibear's Q is now freely available and his E point-and-click stun competes directly with yours for lane control. You want short trades only — Tongue Lash to slow, one or two autos for stacks, then back off before his W bite heal and passive storm procs snowball the extended fight in his favour. Do not activate Thick Skin into a trade you are winning; save it for his all-in so the shield eats his empowered-auto burst and you walk out healthy. At level 6 both of you gain map threats — your Abyssal Voyage lets you roam or reposition globally, but his R disabled-tower dive is the more dangerous immediate threat: if he has ult and you are under 60% health near your tower, respect it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the honest part of this matchup: Volibear's Q stun is back every 10-12s and his E Sky Splitter slow-and-shield competes directly with yours for lane control. You want short trades only — Tongue Lash to slow, one or two autos for stacks, then back off before his W bite heal and Relentless Storm procs snowball the extended fight in his favour. Do not activate Thick Skin into a trade you are winning; save it for his Q all-in so the shield eats his empowered-auto burst and you walk out healthy. At level 6 both of you gain threats — Abyssal Dive is a 1000-range knockup, not an escape, and his R disabled-tower dive is the more dangerous immediate threat: if he has ult and you are under 60% health near your tower, respect it.

edits.before: In skirmishes and teamfights you become the better frontliner by a narrow margin — your Devour removes Volibear's carries from the fight and your Tongue Lash stun chains into point-and-click lockdown he cannot dodge. He answers by diving your backline under his R shield with E stun to counter-lock your own carries, so this is less a duel and more a race to see whose displacement dictates the teamfight. Heartsteel stacking is the real late-game tiebreaker here: whichever of you took Heartsteel earlier and farmed more is just tankier and hits harder, and in a dead-even game that usually comes down to who snowballed the early stun-Devour punishes into CS leads during laning.
edits.after: In skirmishes and teamfights you become the better frontliner by a narrow margin — your Devour removes Volibear's carries from the fight and your Tongue Lash stun chains into point-and-click lockdown he cannot dodge. He answers by diving your backline on R bonus health with E slow and Q stun to counter-lock your own carries, so this is less a duel and more a race to see whose displacement dictates the teamfight. Heartsteel stacking is the real late-game tiebreaker here: whichever of you took Heartsteel earlier and farmed more is just tankier and hits harder, and in a dead-even game that usually comes down to who snowballed the early three-stack punishes into CS leads during laning.

edits.before: Three stacks lets you stun then Devour him mid-wave — one clean execution here usually burns his Flash and gives you a CS and plate lead for the whole lane.
edits.after: Three stacks buys the Q stun or Devour, never both — the stun consumes all three. Devouring him mid-wave burns his Flash and hands you a CS and plate lead.

edits.before: Both of you have access to stuns now; trade short, activate Thick Skin into his E lockdown rather than his passive procs, and never extend when his W bite heal is freshly recharged.
edits.after: Both of you have stuns now; trade short, pop Thick Skin into his Q stun rather than his E slow, and never extend when Frenzied Maul is off cooldown — that re-bite is up every 5s.

edits.before: His R tower-disable dive is the biggest threat in this window — do not be caught low-health under tower, and use Abyssal Voyage to roam rather than stand pat in a 50-50.
edits.after: His R tower-disable dive is the biggest threat in this window — do not be caught low-health under tower, and keep Abyssal Dive up to knock him off you rather than to escape.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online — Tongue Lash stun into Devour removes Volibear from the wave entirely, burning his Flash or costing him 30-40% of his health bar.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online — spend them on Devour, not the Tongue Lash stun, because the stun eats all three. Devour costs him 30-40% of his health bar.

edits.after: Fish for three An Acquired Taste stacks at max Tongue Lash range, then spend them on Devour rather than the Q stun — the stun consumes all three

edits.before: Use E lightning stun to lock Tahm Kench in place and let passive Stormbringer autos shred through Thick Skin grey health before he can activate the shield
edits.after: Open Q stun into E Sky Splitter slow to pin Tahm Kench and let Relentless Storm autos shred his grey health before he can convert it with Thick Skin

edits.before: Lick Volibear to 3 stacks in short exchanges, Q-stun when his answer is down, and Devour the all-in under your wave.
edits.after: Lick Volibear to 3 stacks in short exchanges, then spend them once — Q-stun to peel, or Devour to delete his all-in.

edits.before: Volibear wastes Thundering Smash (Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.

edits.before: - Volibear Thundering Smash: matchup-defining — His engage. Q-stun/W-dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Volibear Thundering Smash: matchup-defining — his stun-dash, down 12s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5. Track it before every engage. - Frenzied Maul: flat 5s, his heal. - Sky Splitter: flat 16s slow. - Devour: kill windows only.

notes: CHAMPION-WIDE, affects far more than this matchup: the phrase "Abyssal Voyage" appears in 26 places across the 9 tahmkench entries I audited (volibear, warwick, wukong, yasuo, yone, yorick, zac, ziggs — content.mid and content.whys[4] in almost every one). Abyssal Voyage was removed in the 2020 rework; the current W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s. The near-miss name detector never flagged it because the string is not close to any live ability name. Worth a repo-wide grep across all champ-data/content/*.js, not just tahmkench. SECOND CHAMPION-WIDE ISSUE: the stock phrase "Q-stun into Devour" / "stun then Devour" is mechanically impossible — Riot's own Q text says the 3 stacks are CONSUMED by the stun, and the passive says 3 stacks are what allows Devour. Three stacks is one charge spent on one of the two. This phrasing is templated across the tahmkench set and should be swept globally.
